name: Nantes Atlantique Airport
before:
The main airport for Nantes, 8 km south west of the city in Bouguenais, and busier than most regional French airports at just over 7.2 million passengers in 2019.

The terminal is a single L shaped building split into four numbered halls. Halls 1 to 3 form the long side across two floors, with check in and baggage claim downstairs and the departure lounges above. Hall 4 is a later single storey building set at a right angle and joined by a lobby, so clients should check which hall their flight uses rather than assuming one entrance.

A separate freight terminal sits to the south with 6,000 square metres of storage.

The airport shares its site with an Airbus factory, which builds the centre wing box for the Airbus fleet and works in composite materials. It is run by the Nantes chamber of commerce rather than a national operator.
after:
The main airport for Nantes, 8 km south west of the city in Bouguenais, and busier than most regional French airports, with about 7.2 million passengers in 2025. It is run by Vinci Airports through its subsidiary Aéroports du Grand Ouest.

The terminal is split into halls, so clients should check which hall their flight uses. Vinci Airports says a building linking the halls, due to open in 2027, will let passengers move between them without going outside.

claims.note: Was 'just over 7.2 million passengers in 2019'. UAF (figures supplied by the operators) gives 7,189,480 for 2025 and Eurostat 7,175,680, 0.2 per cent apart; both round to 7.2 million. Vinci's own airport page shows '7,1M', which reads as the same figure cut short rather than a different count, since the UAF figure is the one the operator itself reported. Air Journal (October 2025) had forecast that 2025 might pass 7.2 million.

claims.note: Was 'run by the Nantes chamber of commerce rather than a national operator', which Wikipedia's own body text still says (its infobox has AGO). The concession company AGO is 85 per cent Vinci Airports; the chamber of commerce (CCI Nantes Saint-Nazaire) holds 10 per cent. The French AIP names AGO as the aerodrome administration.
